candidates.title: Coat-of-Arms of Death, from "The Dance of Death"
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Heraldic shield with a skull, like a tradesman's sign: the undertaker's craft as a coat of arms. Ironic memento mori that matches Pushkin's deadpan tone and Adrian's signboard with the Cupid and inverted torch; reads at thumbnail size. It does not show the dream device or the waking-up ending.

candidates.title: Мыши кота погребают (The Mice Bury the Cat)
candidates.museum: Wikimedia Commons (scan of D. Rovinsky, «Русские народные картинки»)
candidates.why: A Russian folk-print funeral procession played as farce. Same register as the undertaker's housewarming, recognisable to a Russian reader. Crop 2:3 on the cat-on-sledge group; black-and-white line art takes a duotone well.
candidates.caveat: Line reproduction from an 1881 book with typeset caption below; busy composition — crop tight on the procession (focal 40/30) and zoom ~1.5×. Weakest pick; B only.

candidates.title: Двери Тимура (Тамерлана) / Doors of Tamerlane
candidates.museum: State Tretyakov Gallery (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: Nearly a literal illustration of the parable: two motionless guards in front of a monumental closed door. Portrait format, strong symmetry, survives a 2:3 crop with no loss. Does not show the doorkeeper's final words.

candidates.title: The Drawbridge, from "Carceri d'invenzione" (Imaginary Prisons)
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Piranesi's Imaginary Prisons: endless stairs, bridges and gates leading nowhere, the bureaucratic infinity behind the first door. A dense etching, so it works as a monochrome plate under glass.

candidates.title: Schloss Milkel in Moonlight
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A single warm window in a dark house at night: the lamp on the windowsill that the plot hangs on. Portrait, centred, high contrast. A calm, hopeful night scene, not a gloomy one.

candidates.title: Reading by Lamplight
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A figure reading under a lamp: the long evenings spent by the lamp, kept quiet. Etching, takes tinting well.

candidates.title: Das Ballsouper (Supper at the Ball)
candidates.museum: Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin (image via Wikimedia Commons / Google Art Project)
candidates.why: Candles, gilding and a suffocating crush: the glittering, slightly feverish ball Odoevsky describes ('тонкий чад… над бесчисленными тускнеющими свечами'). Crop on the chandelier and the crowd below it. No skeletons, so no spoiler.

candidates.title: The Masked Ball
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: Gavarni's masked ball of 1834, the same year as Odoevsky's text (1833). Faces half-hidden in a dense crowd hint at 'what is under the masks' without showing it. Portrait lithograph.

candidates.title: Palm Tree, Nassau
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: One palm, a strip of shore, the sea: the desert-island premise reduced to a single deadpan sign. Portrait watercolour with a clean silhouette; fits the dry satirical tone.

candidates.title: A Ship in a Stormy Sea
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Aivazovsky's ship in a storm: the shipwreck the story opens with, by the most Russian of marine painters. Small oil sketch; crop on the ship.

candidates.title: Woman at a Balcony
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A richly dressed woman at a carved balcony looking down: the princess in the arena box, with an unreadable gesture. Portrait, no tiger, so it preserves the open question.

candidates.title: Royal Tiger
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Delacroix's 'Royal Tiger' lithograph: the beast already named in the hook, at rest and waiting. A horizontal print, so crop on the head; as a monochrome plate it pairs well with a gold title.

candidates.title: The Cats' Rendezvous
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: Black cat and white cat meeting on the rooftops at night, poster-graphic. Uncanny but playful, like the story's 'creeping' dread. Portrait, central motif.

candidates.title: Pilgrimage to the Torinomachi Festival across the Ricefields of Asakusa (Asakusa tanbo Torinomachi mōde), from the series One Hundred Famous  Views of Edo (Meisho Edo hyakkei)
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A white cat on a windowsill watching a distant procession: calm, ancient, observing humans. Vertical ōban print, crops cleanly to 2:3.

candidates.title: Stag Beetle (Hirschkäfer)
candidates.museum: J. Paul Getty Museum (image via Getty Open Content / Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.license: Getty Open Content Program, free of restrictions (PD)
candidates.why: One beetle, monumental, on blank paper: an insect taken with full philosophical seriousness, the joke of Garshin's debating insects. Perfect portrait centre motif.

candidates.title: Study of Capers, Gorse, and a Beetle
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Merian's botanical study with a beetle on the stem: the 'under the cherry tree' garden world at insect scale. Light, airy, portrait.

candidates.title: Lane Scene at Night
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: A wet country lane at night, bare trees and a single walker: exactly the late return from the station before the drive. Portrait, cinematic, ominous without showing the car or the crash.

candidates.title: The Lonely Tower
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Palmer's moonlit valley with a lone tower: still and uneasy, an English night landscape. Horizontal etching, so crop around the moon and the tower.

candidates.title: Aurora Borealis
candidates.museum: Smithsonian American Art Museum (image via Wikimedia Commons / Google Art Project)
candidates.license: Public domain (PD-Art; author d. 1900); SAAM image released under Smithsonian Open Access (CC0)
candidates.why: The story's celebration happens at the poles, at the 'Electro-Earth-Magnetic' stations; an aurora over polar ice is its setting, with a sense of the future. Crop on the aurora's crown.
candidates.caveat: si.edu returned 403 to scripted checks, so confirm the object-level CC0 flag in a browser.

candidates.title: Nocturne in Black and Gold – The Falling Rocket
candidates.museum: Detroit Institute of Arts (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: Fireworks falling over a dark night: New Year's Eve, the toast, sparks dissolving. Portrait, abstract enough to feel modern on a glass UI.

candidates.title: Frau am Fenster (Woman at a Window)
candidates.museum: Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin (image via Wikimedia Commons / Google Art Project)
candidates.why: A woman with her back to us, gazing out of an opened window: waiting and watching the outside, the aunt's posture in the story. Portrait, quiet, ironic in context. No hunters in the frame.
candidates.headStatus: 200 image/jpeg 8485626 (re-confirmed 200 after the 600 s cooldown; an immediate re-check had returned 429 because upload.wikimedia.org rate-limits scripted bursts)

candidates.title: Udsigt fra kunstnerens vindue
candidates.museum: SMK – Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen
candidates.why: A window opened wide onto light from inside a calm domestic room. The ordinary open window that the niece turns into a ghost story. Portrait, bright, legible.

candidates.title: The Penitent Magdalen
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Candle, mirror, skull and a figure in meditation: séance-and-mortality imagery played straight, which suits a parody of a spiritist scare. Portrait, strong chiaroscuro, wow at any size.

candidates.title: Figure Reading at a Table in an Interior at Night
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A figure reading at a table under a lamp at night. It matches the hook ('дочитал это при всех включённых лампах'). Charcoal, dark and soft; titles go on top.

candidates.title: A Home in the Wilderness
candidates.museum: The Cleveland Museum of Art
candidates.why: A lonely settler's cabin under mountains in the wilderness at dusk: the frontier isolation of Bierce's Ohio forest, 1830. Horizontal: crop off-centre on the cabin and the shoreline. The animal does not appear.
candidates.caveat: Cabin sits left of centre, so the 2:3 crop must be offset.

candidates.title: In the Woods
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Dense primeval forest, tall and dark: the 'вековой лес' that swallows the hermit's life. Portrait; strong vertical trunks frame a title.
candidates.caveat: Use the Met's additionalImages[0] (C_034R4.jpg); primaryImage is only 825×1024.

candidates.title: Kellar (magician's poster)
candidates.museum: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: A stage magician in tails with little red imps around him: the 'никакого обмана' charm with a hint of menace. Bold chromolithograph, portrait, reads instantly.
candidates.headStatus: 200 image/jpeg 3962046 (re-confirmed 200 after the 600 s cooldown; an immediate re-check had returned 429 because upload.wikimedia.org rate-limits scripted bursts)

candidates.title: The Magic Lantern
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Silhouette of a family watching a magic-lantern show: a father and child in front of wonders, the story's own pair (narrator and Gip). Crop on the beam and the children.

candidates.title: The Card Players
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Cézanne's card players: the same people at the same table, year after year. Crop on the central player and the table; the most recognisable card-game image in Western art.

candidates.title: The Card Player
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: Rembrandt's single card player studying his hand: the private hope for the perfect deal. Portrait etching with a centred figure.

candidates.title: An Icy Night, New York
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: New York, night, ice, gaslight through the trees: the cold, empty street where the meeting is set for 10 p.m. Photogravure with a cinematic, non-spoiling mood.
candidates.caveat: Author d. 1946 (PD in life+70 since 2017). The Met marks its Stieglitz prints as not open access; AIC marks this one is_public_domain=true.

candidates.title: New York Street
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: A turn-of-century New York street with lamp posts and a lone figure: period and place, warmer tone. Portrait.

candidates.title: Gudgeon and Shark, from "The Comic Natural History of the Human Race"
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: 'Gudgeon and Shark', literally: a small fish and its predator, from a 19th-c. satirical natural history. Matches Shchedrin's fable-satire exactly. Centre crop on the fish.
candidates.caveat: Printed caption 'GUDGEON SHARK' sits inside a full-height 2:3 crop. Zoom ~1.25× (e.g. `scale: 1.25` on the img) or accept it as a period label.

candidates.title: Carp
candidates.museum: Art Institute of Chicago
candidates.why: One fish, vertical, monumental, on blue water: the solitary fish life of the fable as a bold graphic. Portrait print that crops to 2:3 almost natively.

candidates.title: Udsigt gennem et vindue på Procida
candidates.museum: SMK – Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen
candidates.why: A view of the Mediterranean through a window: the story opens with an investigator looking through a barred window at the glittering sea and the Pisan hills. Portrait, light, Italian.

candidates.title: Armor
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Redon's head locked in a helmet: a mind enclosed by an apparatus, a metaphor for the thought-reading device. Dark, centred, surreal; the irony comes through the title.

candidates.title: Study of a Hand
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A single hand drawn in red chalk on cream paper, isolated like a trophy on a wall. Elegant, uncanny, centred. It shows no attack and no chain.

candidates.title: Study of Hands
candidates.museum: The Cleveland Museum of Art
candidates.why: Ingres's sheet of hand studies: anatomical, detached hands on blank paper, quietly disturbing. Portrait.

candidates.title: Red Sunset
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A blood-red sunset under a black cloud. The narrator's first line is 'Больше всего я ненавижу солнце', and the red sun points to the title. A Russian painter in a CC0 collection, with an obvious centred motif.

candidates.title: Купание красного коня / Bathing of a Red Horse
candidates.museum: State Tretyakov Gallery (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.license: Public domain (PD-Art; author d. 1939, PD in RU/EU since 2010; published 1912, PD in US)
candidates.why: A red horse and a young rider: the brother who rode off with the cavalry, rendered as a near-icon of revolutionary Russia. Strong red mass; crop on the horse's head and the rider.
candidates.caveat: Commons file is only 1672×1471, so the 2:3 crop is ~980×1471 px (fine for cards, soft for full-screen hero). Rider is nude.

candidates.title: Interiør. Den gamle bilæggerovn. Albertines Lyst, Lyngby
candidates.museum: SMK – Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen
candidates.why: An empty room with an old iron stove standing like an idol. Zamyatin's tenants 'молятся чугунной печке'. Portrait, Hammershøi's cold grey light, which is very current.

candidates.title: Das Eismeer (The Sea of Ice)
candidates.museum: Hamburger Kunsthalle (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: The story opens 'Ледники, мамонты, пустыни': a petrified ice age. Friedrich's pyramid of ice slabs is that metaphor. Crop on the ice wedge.
candidates.caveat: Commons file 2048×1552, so the 2:3 crop is ~1035×1552 px.

candidates.title: Madame X (Virginie Amélie Avegno Gautreau)
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A pale, aristocratic woman in black against a dark ground, beautiful and slightly wrong. The 'гостья' before we know what she is. Portrait, iconic, no fangs or gore.

candidates.title: Неизвестная (Portrait of an Unknown Woman)
candidates.museum: State Tretyakov Gallery (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: The most famous enigmatic woman in Russian painting, in a winter Petersburg setting that matches the святочный frame. She looks down at the viewer: alluring, unknowable.
candidates.caveat: Commons file 2048×1543, so the 2:3 crop is ~1029×1543 px. Very well known; may read as 'chocolate-box' to some readers.

candidates.title: Степь. Нива (Steppe. Cornfield)
candidates.museum: Yaroslavl Art Museum (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: An endless southern steppe under a high sky, with a single figure walking the road: the young teacher heading to her village. Light mood, Russian painter. Crop around the figure.
candidates.headStatus: 200 image/jpeg 1200399 (re-confirmed 200 after the 600 s cooldown; an immediate re-check had returned 429 because upload.wikimedia.org rate-limits scripted bursts)

candidates.title: Сосны, освещённые солнцем (Pines Lit by the Sun)
candidates.museum: State Tretyakov Gallery (image via Wikimedia Commons)
candidates.why: Sunlit pines on sandy ground: the greening of the sands the teacher fights for, warm and hopeful. Portrait, crops natively.
candidates.caveat: Commons file 1461×2048: enough for cards, borderline for a full-bleed hero.

candidates.title: The Ridotto Pubblico at Palazzo Dandolo
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: A Venetian ridotto full of masked revellers under a vast ceiling: the prince's sealed-off party without the intruder. Horizontal, so crop on the central masked group; the ceiling gives headroom for the title.

candidates.title: The Masque of the Red Death, for Edgar Allan Poe’s “Tales of Mystery and the Imagination,” Chicago, 1895–96
candidates.museum: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
candidates.why: Beardsley's own drawing for this tale: black-and-white Art Nouveau elegance, an unmistakable masquerade silhouette, high wow at small sizes.
candidates.caveat: SPOILER RISK, medium: it depicts the masked intruder, the story's midnight climax (not the final line). Use only if the title is already visible; otherwise prefer the Guardi.
